searchText: Sync participation is in line with attestation participation it seems to me both are there at 95% right? that's a very healthy signal eth1 voting (I know nothing weird was supposed to happen here) is still perfect, with 556 for the first hash, 4 for the second and just 4 random hashes, I don't remember seeing such a nice vote on mainnet quick question.. and pls correct me where I am wrong on this.. i believe prior to altair, block proposals were "credited" two epochs later... post-altair, it appears like it is the next epoch.. (same for attestations).. did something chnage? or was my understanding off.. happy to get some wisdom ! thx.. proposer attestation and sync committee inclusion reawards are done at the exact block as are sync committee rewards to that committee attestation rewards for activity in epoch N are still rewarded at the end of epoch N+1 (and in phase 0, proposer rewards were batched at epoch boundaries like attesation rewards but no longer as noted above) thank you ! Seems that a lot of missed blocks are from validators that look healthy based on their attestations performance ( https://beaconcha.in/validator/223385 https://beaconcha.in/validator/153841 https://beaconcha.in/validator/203050 https://beaconcha.in/validator/121419 ) . Is there a known reason? From what I can tell various operators did not properly configure/upgrade their remote signer and/or validator client setup the crux here is that the `Attestation` type did not change (and so legacy signing entities can handle the altair attestations) whereas the `BeaconBlock` type did (thus legacy signing software was borked) I think a lesson to be learnt from this event is that clients need to purposely brick their legacy signer, be it remote, or local, when a fork comes some (many) institutions use their own remote signer it implies that these institutions did *minimal if not zero* testing on altair testnets I would suspect they saw a good attestation % nubmer and said "we're good to go" or just didn't run on testnets at all From the fixes I've seen being applied on repos I'd suspect is a stock signer. But yeah, failing to propose should pass CI in case of clients and a test on testnets in case of large users
